what: HIGH (code audit CA-A05-004, MEASURED 2026-09-27): LiquidityDetector.detect_liquidity_sweeps() (src/ict_detection/liquidity.py:120-159) implements only half its own documented contract. Its docstring (lines 121-126) defines a sweep as "Price pierces through the liquidity level, Then quickly reverses (takes the liquidity and runs)" -- but the implementation only checks the pierce half (`if candle_high > pool["price"]: pool["swept"]=True; break` / the mirrored low check), with zero check for a subsequent reversal anywhere in the function. Reproduced with a synthetic 40-bar series: a 2-touch equal-high pool at 100.0, price breaks above 100 at bar 25 and trends monotonically upward for 15 more bars (never reversing) -- flagged swept=True at bar 25 regardless. tests/test_liquidity.py has exactly one sweep test and never exercises the reversal half, so this was never caught. This feeds /api/bot/liquidity's recent_sweeps array on the operator-facing "Liquidity Maps" dashboard tab (src/runtime/liquidity_state.py -> src/web/api/routers/liquidity.py) -- no live strategy reads this back (write-only from strategy_signal_builders.py, read-only by the web API), so this is a dashboard-accuracy issue today, not an order-routing issue, but it means the operator-visible liquidity map has been silently over-reporting stop-run sweeps as "break of level" events with no distinction, for as long as this detector has been live. FIX: either correct the docstring to say "break of level" (matching current behavior), or add a real reversal check (e.g. close back on the origin side within N bars) before setting swept=True, and add a test exercising the no-reversal case. Full finding: docs/audits/code-audit-2026-09-27/CA-A05.findings.jsonl id CA-A05-004.
